overview: Brunei is a small country on the north coast of the island of Borneo, split into two parts by Malaysia. Its capital is Bandar Seri Begawan. Brunei is ruled by a sultan and became independent from the United Kingdom in 1984. Oil and gas have made it one of the wealthiest countries in Asia.

geography.text: Brunei faces the South China Sea, and most of the country is covered by tropical rainforest, much of it protected. The capital is famous for Kampong Ayer, a 'water village' of houses built on stilts over the Brunei River.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Hot and humid all year, with heavy rain.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Proboscis monkeys, with their long noses, live in the mangroves.

history.text: In the 1400s and 1500s the Sultanate of Brunei controlled much of Borneo and parts of the southern Philippines. Its territory shrank greatly in the 1800s, and it became a British protectorate in 1888. Oil was found in 1929, and Brunei became fully independent in 1984.

events.title: Height of the sultanate
events.text: Brunei's power stretches across Borneo and into the Philippines.

government.text: Brunei is an absolute monarchy. The Sultan is head of state, Prime Minister, finance minister and defence minister. Hassanal Bolkiah has reigned since 1967. There are no national elections, and Islamic law is applied alongside common law.

economy.text: Oil and natural gas make up most of Brunei's exports and government income. Brunei has no income tax, and citizens receive free healthcare and education. The government is trying to grow other industries.

culture.text: Brunei is a Malay Muslim monarchy. Kampong Ayer, a 'water village' of houses on stilts, has existed for centuries. The Sultan's palace, Istana Nurul Iman, is one of the largest residential palaces in the world.

items.title: Kampong Ayer
items.text: Thousands of people live in houses on stilts over the river.

items.title: Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque
items.text: A golden-domed mosque in a lagoon.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Ambuyat, a sticky starch from the sago palm, eaten with sauces.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Brassware and silverwork, especially ceremonial cannons and pots.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: On the Sultan's birthday, the country celebrates with parades and fireworks.

sport.text: Football and badminton are popular, and silat, a Malay martial art, is practised widely. Brunei sends small teams to the Olympics.

items.title: Silat
items.text: A martial art practised across the Malay world, listed by UNESCO.

didYouKnow: Brunei's Sultan lives in Istana Nurul Iman, one of the world's largest palaces, with about 1,800 rooms.
Brunei has no personal income tax.
